# Contributing

Thank you for your interest in contributing to this repository.

This repository supports the teaching process of the **Reinforced Concrete Design II**
course. Contributions are welcome when they improve the accuracy of the theory,
the clarity of the notebooks, the correctness of the computational tools, or the
overall documentation.

## How You Can Contribute

You may contribute in the following ways:

- Reporting errors or inconsistencies in the theory notebooks, examples, or the
  `repo__CORE_concreteII_desing` package
- Pointing out mismatches with the current **ACI CODE-318-25** provisions or the
  **Norma Ecuatoriana de la Construcción (NEC)**
- Suggesting clarifications to explanations, derivations, or notation
- Improving readability, comments, or formatting of notebooks and code
- Submitting pull requests for well-scoped corrections or improvements

## Before Contributing

Before opening a pull request, please make sure that:

- The proposed change is clearly described
- The contribution is relevant to the educational scope of the course
- Notebooks remain runnable from top to bottom without errors
- New material is consistent with the notation and style already used in the
  repository
- Any change to a design criterion, formula, or code reference is discussed
  first through an issue

## Issues

If you find a bug, inconsistency, or mistake, please open an issue and include:

- A clear description of the problem
- The notebook, file, or section where it appears
- The relevant ACI CODE-318-25 (or NEC) section, if applicable
- A suggested correction, if available

## Pull Requests

Pull requests are welcome for focused and meaningful improvements.

Please ensure that pull requests:

- Address a specific issue or improvement
- Do not introduce unnecessary complexity
- Keep notebooks executable and consistent with the rest of the course material
- Are written as clearly as possible

## Important Note for Students

This repository is maintained exclusively by the course authors. Students are
expected to clone the repository and update their local copies during the
semester rather than modify the original repository directly. If you wish to
experiment with the code, please do so in your local copy or in a personal fork.

The official development and organization of the repository remain under the
supervision of the authors. Suggestions for improvement may still be shared
through issues or pull requests, which will be reviewed before any change is
incorporated into the repository.

## Final Note

The maintainers reserve the right to review, revise, or decline contributions in
order to preserve the technical accuracy and educational coherence of the
repository.

Thank you for helping improve this project.
